correctness.rationale: Laurent (1996, §4.3) supplies the requisite complete 32-vertex MET_5 classification: 16 cut vertices and 16 switching-equivalent fractional vertices a_S=(2/3)1−δ(S)/3. A maximum five-vertex cut has six edges; averaging the ten maximum-size cuts gives b_∅=(3/5)1∈CUT_5. Every cut mixture has total edge sum at most 6, while ∑a_∅=20/3; Hölder enforces distance ≥(2/3)/10^{1−1/p}=10^{1/p}/15. Residual a_∅−b_∅=1/15 on all ten coordinates attains it for all p; switching transfers to all sixteen a_S. Convexifying nearest approximants to every MET vertex supplies global upper bound. For finite p>1 strict convexity, and for p=1 opposite coordinate signs of any two distinct switched residuals, enforce precisely those sixteen farthest vertices. Support-function/Hölder duality then gives 16 normal directions c_S=10^(−1/q)(1−2δ(S)) for p<∞, with no p∞ uniqueness claim. Independently checked all 16 rational projection normal inequalities and exact squared Euclidean gap 2/45. The full vertex exhaustiveness is genuinely from Laurent 1996, not floating-point census.

originality.rationale: The 32-vertex list, metric switchings and cut framework are fully credited to Laurent (1996). The proposed new content is exact all-ℓp distance and the complete primal/dual extremizer classification. Deza–Laurent–Poljak (1992) investigates triangle facets and cut/metric relative positioning, and Deza–Dutour Sikirić (2017) generalizes cut/metric polytopes; the full formula is not found in the material read. The max-cut relaxation alias is explicitly equivalent and not claimed as a separate novelty. Older integrality-gap literature may already imply the formula and remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: An older max-cut relaxation integrality-gap or metric/cut polytope paper may give the same sharp normalized support gap under different normalization.
The full 1992 Deza–Laurent–Poljak article and 2017 generalized framework were not materially read in full, so no whole-document exclusion is asserted.
Farthest and dual equality classifications claimed only for finite p; p=∞ multiplicity not addressed.

value.rationale: MET_5 is the first complete-graph metric relaxation not equal to CUT_5. The all-norm sharp Hausdorff and support gaps, simultaneous nearest cut mixtures, and complete finite-p equality sets quantify a natural global max-cut/metric relaxation defect at the smallest nontrivial order. It is independently useful even though the 32-vertex classification is already known; it is not merely re-enumerating the vertices.
